'''Wolfgang Martin Heckl''' (born 10 September 1958 in [[Parsberg]], [[Upper Palatinate]]) is a German [[biophysicist]], [[experimental physicist]] and science administrator. His research has focused on [[nanoscience]], [[scanning probe microscopy]] and [[science communication]]. From 2004 to 2025 he was Director General of the [[Deutsches Museum]] in [[Munich]], and from 2009 to 2025 he held the Oskar von Miller Chair of Science Communication at the [[Technical University of Munich]].<ref name="tum2025">{{cite web |title=Deutsches Museum continues its successful development under the leadership of a TUM professor |url=https://www.tum.de/en/news-and-events/all-news/press-releases/details/michael-decker-ist-neuer-generaldirektor |publisher=Technical University of Munich |date=2025 |access-date=14 October 2026}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
After completing his [[Abitur]] with a grade average of 1.0 (the best possible grade; his total score would arithmetically correspond to a theoretical average of 0.8)<ref>{{cite web |title=Physiker Wolfgang M. Heckl – Die Kultur der Reparatur |url=https://www.deutschlandfunkkultur.de/physiker-wolfgang-m-heckl-die-kultur-der-reparatur.970.de.html?dram:article_id=393545 |website=Deutschlandfunk Kultur | date=16 August 2017 |language=de |access-date=19 November 2017}}</ref> at the Ostendorfer-Gymnasium in [[Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz]], Heckl studied physics at the [[Technical University of Munich]] from 1978 to 1985. In 1988 he obtained his doctorate (Dr. rer. nat.) at the Institute of Biophysics in Munich with a thesis on the lateral organisation of [[lipid]] monolayers under the influence of [[amphiphile|amphiphilic]] foreign substances and [[protein]]s. He then worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Toronto]] and in the [[IBM]] research group of [[Gerd Binnig]]. In 1993 he completed his [[habilitation]] in physics at [[LMU Munich]] with a thesis on [[scanning tunneling microscopy]] of two-dimensional crystals of organic molecules, and subsequently accepted a professorship at LMU.

In the same year Heckl received the Philip Morris Research Prize for his work on the structural elucidation of the [[nucleobase|DNA bases]], and was entered in the ''[[Guinness World Records|Guinness Book of Records]]'' for writing an atomic bit, under the title "the world's smallest hole".{{citation needed|date=October 2026}}

Heckl is a full member of the Center for NanoScience (CeNS) and the GeoBio-Center of LMU Munich, of the [[Nanosystems Initiative Munich]] (NIM), and of the [[acatech|German Academy of Science and Engineering (acatech)]], among other organisations. He has served on numerous bodies, including as chairman of the board of trustees of the [[Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics]], as a jury member for the [[Deutscher Zukunftspreis|German Future Prize]] and the [[Deutscher Umweltpreis|German Environmental Prize]], and as a board member of the [[Eduard Rhein Foundation]]. He has also advised the [[European Commission]] and the [[Federal Government of Germany|German federal government]] on [[nanotechnology]].

In 2004 Heckl became Director General of the [[Deutsches Museum]]. He was responsible for the museum's difficult modernisation and for its ambitious plans to expand to [[Nuremberg]]. He was criticised for the costly measures at the museum's transport centre (''Verkehrszentrum'') on the Theresienhöhe.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Krass |first1=Sebastian |last2=Scherf |first2=Martina |title=150 Millionen Euro für Sanierung des Deutschen Museums |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/muenchen/deutsches-museum-sanierung-kosten-1.4436050 |newspaper=[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] |language=de |access-date=4 August 2019}}</ref> In 2009 he accepted an appointment to the [[Oskar von Miller]] Chair of Science Communication at the Technical University of Munich (School of Education / Physics Department). Heckl retired at the end of May 2025 after more than 20 years as Director General, longer than any of his predecessors; he was succeeded on 1 June 2025 by the physicist Michael Decker, who also took over the TUM chair.<ref name="tum2025" />

In December 2025 the Technical University of Munich conferred on Heckl the honorary title ''TUM Emeritus of Excellence'', making him a member of the TUM Senior Excellence Faculty.<ref>{{cite web |title=Exzellente Verstärkung: Sechs neue TUM Emeriti of Excellence im Jahr 2025 |url=https://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/eoe/news-single-view/article/exzellente-verstaerkung-fuenf-neue-tum-emeriti-of-excellence-im-jahr-2024-1/ |publisher=TUM Senior Excellence Faculty |date=1 December 2025 |language=de |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref> <ref>{{cite web |title=TUM Emeriti of Excellence – Übersicht nach Ernennungsjahr |url=https://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/eoe/tum-emeriti-of-excellence-eoe/portraits-nach-ernennungsjahr/ |publisher=TUM Senior Excellence Faculty |language=de |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref>

Heckl also chairs the international jury of the [[European Inventor Award]] of the [[European Patent Office]].<ref>{{cite press release |title=Recognising inventors that transform our world and our lives: European Inventor Award 2023 finalists announced |url=https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/press-centre/press-release/2023/476914 |publisher=European Patent Office |date=9 May 2023 |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=About the award |url=https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/european-inventor-award/about-award |publisher=European Patent Office |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release |title=Unveiling excellence: European Inventor Award 2024 finalists revealed |url=https://www.epo.org/en/news-events/press-centre/press-release/2024/1147736 |publisher=European Patent Office |date=16 May 2024 |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref>

Heckl is married to the lawyer Sigrid Schütz-Heckl; they have one daughter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. rer. nat. habil. Wolfgang M. Heckl – Curriculum Vitae |url=https://www.deutsches-museum.de/assets/Forschung/Forschungsinstitut/Download/Mitarbeiter/Heckl_CV_2021_webDMlong.pdf |publisher=Deutsches Museum |year=2021 |language=de |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref>

== Public engagement ==
From 2007 to 2018 Heckl was a regular guest on the [[Bayerischer Rundfunk|Bavarian Television]] programme ''Der Sonntags-Stammtisch''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sonntags-Stammtisch: Aus für Heckl und Hanitzsch |url=https://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/inhalt.br-sendung-sonntags-stammtisch-aus-fuer-heckl-und-hanitzsch.9da830ec-7f22-49d6-8847-a3ebf60fc589.html |newspaper=[[Abendzeitung]] |date=6 December 2018 |language=de |access-date=10 December 2018}}</ref> He writes the column ''Hier schreibt Heckl'' ("Heckl writes here") for ''[[P.M. Magazin]]''.

In August 2013 he published the book ''Die Kultur der Reparatur'' ("The Culture of Repair"), in which he promotes [[repair]] as a way out of [[planned obsolescence|obsolescence]] and the [[throwaway society]]. In an interview he said that he meets regularly with the astronaut [[Ulrich Walter]] to repair old television sets.<ref>''[[Süddeutsche Zeitung]]'', no. 98, 27/28 April 2013, p. 31. See also: {{cite magazine |last=Frasch |first=Timo |title=Interview with Wolfgang M. Heckl |magazine=Frankfurter Allgemeine Magazin |url=https://dynamic.faz.net/download/2020/fazmagazin_202010.pdf |date=October 2020 |page=47 |language=de}}</ref> He opened a [[repair café]] in [[Farchant]].<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Frasch |first=Timo |title=Interview with Wolfgang M. Heckl |magazine=Frankfurter Allgemeine Magazin |url=https://dynamic.faz.net/download/2020/fazmagazin_202010.pdf |date=October 2020 |page=48 |language=de}}</ref>

In an interview with the radio station WDR 3 in October 2026, Heckl explained why he regards repair as a cultural practice: for thousands of years repair had been an integral part of human life, not least because material goods were scarce and valuable; moreover, it was a general principle of nature, since life could neither have arisen nor persisted without molecular repair mechanisms, and humans should carry this principle over into technological society.<ref name="wdr3">{{cite interview |subject=Wolfgang M. Heckl |title=Reparieren als kulturelle Praxis |work=WDR 3 Mosaik |publisher=Westdeutscher Rundfunk |date=12 October 2026 |language=de}}</ref> He noted that his 2013 book had listed about 80 repair cafés in Germany, whereas there are now more than 1,000, and described them as social places for exchanging ideas about how people want to live in the future.<ref name="wdr3"/>

== Art ==
Heckl is also active as an artist. Under the title ''Science & Art'' he translates scientific phenomena into artistic forms, ranging from images of the [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoworld]] and paintings inspired by [[molecule|molecular]] structures to works that use [[artificial intelligence|AI]] algorithms he developed himself to translate images into music and music into images. In 2026 his work was shown in the exhibition ''Science & Art. Von der Molekularkunst zur KI-Kunst'' at the [[Palais Niederösterreich]] in Vienna.<ref>{{cite press release |title="SCIENCE & ART. Von der Molekularkunst zur KI-Kunst": Ausstellung von Wolfgang M. Heckl im Palais Niederösterreich |url=https://noe.gv.at/noe/-SCIENCE_-_ART._Von_der_Molekularkunst_zur_KI-Kunst-_Auss.html |publisher=Amt der NÖ Landesregierung |date=17 July 2026 |language=de |access-date=16 October 2026}}</ref>

His research on atoms and molecules serves as inspiration for his painting; he describes his own visual language as ''Molekülismus'' ("molecularism").<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/eoe/news-single-view/article/science-art-wolfgang-m-heckl-zeigt-seine-gemaelde-in-garmisch-partenkirchen/ |title=Science & Art: Wolfgang M. Heckl zeigt seine Gemälde in Garmisch-Partenkirchen |publisher=Technical University of Munich, TUM Emeriti of Excellence |language=de |access-date=20 October 2026}}</ref> As early as 2002, in the project ''Atomare Klangwelten'' ("Atomic Soundscapes"), he developed a method for translating scanning tunnelling microscope images of atoms and molecules into sound.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.avbstiftung.de/atomare-klangwelten/ |title=Atomare Klangwelten |publisher=Andrea von Braun Stiftung |date=12 April 2002 |language=de |access-date=20 October 2026}}</ref> In 2021, together with K. Wienand, he published a study on translating images into melodies using artificial intelligence (variational autoencoders).<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Wienand |first1=K. |last2=Heckl |first2=W. M. |title=The artificial synesthete: Image-melody translations with variational autoencoders |eprint=2112.02953 |year=2021 |class=cs.CV }}</ref>

Heckl is a member of the Kunstgilde Parsberg, an artists' guild in his home town,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kunstgilde-parsberg.de/mitglieder/aktive-mitglieder |title=Aktive Mitglieder |publisher=Kunstgilde Parsberg |language=de |access-date=20 October 2026}}</ref> and is listed in the ''Werdenfelser Künstlerlexikon''.<ref>{{cite book |last=Benkert |first=Ralf |title=Werdenfelser Künstlerlexikon: Künstlerlexikon des Werdenfelser Landes |year=2003 |language=de}}</ref>

=== Selected solo exhibitions ===
* 2012: ''Moleküle in der Landschaft'' ("Molecules in the Landscape"), Studio La Cave, Munich
* 2018: Walchensee Museum, Urfeld am Walchensee
* 2018: ''Molekülismus'', Neumarkt in der Oberpfalz (13–21 August)
* 2018: Barockschlössl Mistelbach, Lower Austria (24–26 August), marking the 35th anniversary of the town partnership between Neumarkt and Mistelbach<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mistelbach.at/politik-buergerservice/presse/news/news-detail/artikel/generaldirektor-des-deutschen-museums-stellt-in-mi/ |title=Generaldirektor des Deutschen Museums stellt in Mistelbach aus |publisher=Stadtgemeinde Mistelbach |year=2018 |language=de |access-date=20 October 2026}}</ref>
* 2018: ''Science & Art'', Hans Eisenmann Centre, Weihenstephan Science Centre (13–20 October), on the occasion of the 150th anniversary of the Technical University of Munich
* 2024: ''Science & Art'', Mohr-Villa, Munich-Freimann (26 April – 18 May)<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mohrvilla.de/veranstaltung-aus-archiv/ausstellung-science-art.html |title=Ausstellung Science & Art |publisher=Mohr-Villa Freimann |language=de |access-date=20 October 2026}}</ref>
* 2026: ''Science & Art. Von der Molekularkunst zur KI-Kunst'', Palais Niederösterreich, Vienna (17 July – 19 August)

== Awards and honours ==
For his efforts to communicate scientific results to the public, Heckl received the Communicator Prize of the [[Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft]] in 2002, and in 2004 the [[Descartes Prize]] of the [[European Commission]] in the category "Professional scientists engaged in science communication to the public".<ref>{{cite press release |title=EU verleiht Descartes-Preise 2004 für wissenschaftliche Spitzenleistungen |url=http://europa.eu/rapid/press-release_IP-04-1435_de.htm |publisher=European Commission |date=2 December 2004 |language=de |access-date=20 April 2019}}</ref>
* 1993: Philip Morris Research Prize
* 2008: Cross of Merit on Ribbon of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Bundesverdienstorden für Prof. Wolfgang Heckl |url=https://www.geobio-center.uni-muenchen.de/aktuelles/notes/heckl/index.html |publisher=LMU Munich |date=7 April 2008 |language=de |access-date=7 June 2024}}</ref>
* 2015: Ring of Honour of the [[Eduard Rhein Foundation]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Ehrenringträger |url=https://www.eduard-rhein-stiftung.de/preistrager/ehrenring/ |publisher=Eduard-Rhein-Stiftung |language=de |access-date=7 June 2024}}</ref>
* 2020: Arthur Burkhardt Prize<ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur Burkhardt-Stiftung zeichnet Klimaökonom Ottmar Edenhofer und Biophysiker Wolfgang M. Heckl aus |url=https://www.deutsches-stiftungszentrum.de/aktuelles/2021_11_11_arthur_burkhardt-preis |publisher=Deutsches Stiftungszentrum |date=9 November 2021 |language=de |access-date=7 June 2024}}</ref>
* 2024: Officer's Cross (Cross of Merit, 1st Class) of the [[Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Ordensverleihung zum Tag der Deutschen Einheit |url=https://www.bundespraesident.de/SharedDocs/Berichte/DE/Frank-Walter-Steinmeier/2024/10/241001-Verdienstorden-TdDE.html |publisher=Federal President of Germany |language=de |access-date=2 October 2024}}</ref>
* 2025: ''Pro meritis scientiae et litterarum'' of the Bavarian State Ministry of Science and the Arts<ref>{{cite press release |title="Herausragende bayerische Botschafter für Innovation" – Blume ehrt Prof. Dr. Wolfgang M. Heckl, Prof. Dr. Rudolf Gross und Prof. Dr. Helmut Schönenberger mit PRO MERITIS SCIENTIAE ET LITTERARUM |url=https://www.stmwk.bayern.de/pressemitteilung/12951/herausragende-bayerische-botschafter-fuer-innovation-blume-ehrt-prof-dr-wolfgang-m-heckl-prof-dr-rudolf-gross-und-prof-dr-helmut-schoenenberger-mit-pro-meritis-scientiae-et-litterarum.html |publisher=Bavarian State Ministry of Science and the Arts |date=29 October 2025 |language=de |access-date=14 October 2026}}</ref>
